title: Carol Burnett
wiki_lead:
Carol Creighton Burnett (born April 26, 1933) is an American comedienne, actress, singer and writer. Burnett has played dramatic and comedic roles on stage and screen. She has received numerous awards and accolades, including five Golden Globe Awards, a Grammy Award, seven Primetime Emmy Awards, twelve People's Choice Awards, two Peabody Awards. Burnett was honored with a Special Tony Award in 1969, Star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1975, the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2005, the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor in 2013, the Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award in 2015, and the inaugural Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award in 2019.
Burnett was born and raised in San Antonio, Texas, until her family moved to Hollywood, living a block away from Hollywood Boulevard. She attended Hollywood High School and eventually studied theater and musical comedy at UCLA. Later, she moved to New York City, performed in nightclubs there, and had a breakout success on Broadway in 1959 in Once Upon a Mattress, for which she received a Tony Award nomination. She soon made her television debut, regularly appearing on The Garry Moore Show for the next three years, and won her first Emmy Award in 1962.
Eventually, Burnett moved back to Los Angeles and began an 11-year run as star of the CBS variety-sketch comedy series The Carol Burnett Show from 1967 to 1978. She is the first woman to host a comedy-variety series. With its vaudeville roots, The Carol Burnett Show was a variety show that combined comedy sketches with song and dance. The comedy sketches included film parodies and character pieces. Burnett created many memorable characters during the show's run, and both she and the show won numerous Emmy and Golden Globe Awards. 
Burnett's film roles include Pete 'n' Tillie (1972), The Front Page (1974), A Wedding (1978), The Four Seasons (1981), Annie (1982), Noises Off (1992), and Horton Hears a Who! (2008). On television, she won an Emmy Award for her guest role in Mad About You. She appeared in multiple specials with Julie Andrews. She was nominated for a Tony for her role in Moon Over Buffalo (1995). Recently she has acted in Better Call Saul (2022), Palm Royale (2024), and Hacks (2025). She recorded her memoir In Such Good Company (2016), for which she won a Grammy Award. 
In 2019, the Golden Globes created the Carol Burnett Award for career achievement in television, giving Burnett the first award. She was honored with an NBC special Carol Burnett: 90 Years of Laughter + Love celebrating her 90th birthday.

Early life and education

Carol Creighton Burnett was born on April 26, 1933, at Nix Hospital in San Antonio, Texas, the daughter of Ina Louise (née Creighton), a publicity writer for movie studios, and Joseph Thomas Burnett, a movie theater manager. grok_lead: Carol Burnett (born Carol Creighton Burnett; April 26, 1933) is an American actress, comedian, singer, and writer, best known for her groundbreaking work in television comedy as the star and host of the variety-sketch series The Carol Burnett Show from 1967 to 1978. Born in San Antonio, Texas, she was raised primarily by her grandmother in a one-room apartment in Hollywood, California, after her parents separated due to alcoholism. After graduating from Hollywood High School in 1951, Burnett attended the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), where she studied theater arts and English on a donor-funded scholarship, eventually leaving to pursue a performing career in New York City. Burnett's breakthrough came in 1959 with her Tony-nominated performance as Princess Winnifred in the Broadway musical Once Upon a Mattress, which led to her becoming a regular performer on The Garry Moore Show from 1959 to 1962, earning her first Primetime Emmy Award in 1962 for Outstanding Performance in a Variety or Musical Program or Series. She transitioned to her own CBS variety series, The Carol Burnett Show, which ran for 11 seasons and featured ensemble cast members including Harvey Korman, Vicki Lawrence, Lyle Waggoner, and Tim Conway, blending sketch comedy, musical numbers, and celebrity guest appearances while pioneering formats like the Q&A audience interaction segment. The show received widespread acclaim for its innovative humor and Burnett's versatile improvisational style, amassing 25 Emmy Awards during its run and establishing her as a television icon. Throughout her career, Burnett has earned seven Primetime Emmy Awards personally, including wins for her work on The Carol Burnett Show and a 2024 nomination for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series for her role as Norma Dellacorte in Palm Royale, making her the oldest acting nominee in Emmy history at age 91. She has also secured five Golden Globe Awards, a Peabody Award, the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2005, the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor in 2013, and the Screen Actors Guild Life Achievement Award in 2017. In addition to television, Burnett has appeared in films such as Annie (1982) and The Front Page (1974), starred in the sitcom Mama's Family (1983â1990), and continued performing on stage and in guest roles on series like Better Call Saul (2018â2022), the 2023 NBC special Carol Burnett: 90 Years of Laughter + Love honoring her 90th birthday, and the second season of Palm Royale (2025), while in 2025 donating her collection of over 140 awards to UCLA to establish a scholarship, and authoring memoirs including In Such Good Company (2016). Her enduring contributions to comedy have been honored with the eponymous Carol Burnett Award for Television Excellence, first presented to her by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association in 2019.
